questions.stem: On a modern smartphone, device encryption is usually on by default. What acts as the key to that encrypted data?
questions.explanation: On modern phones, encryption is usually enabled by default and the passcode/PIN acts as the key to unlock the data.
questions.trap: The IMEI is a public hardware identifier, not a secret key; it does not protect encrypted data.

questions.stem: Among the mobile screen-lock options, which is described as the LEAST secure?
questions.explanation: A simple swipe provides essentially no authentication, making it the least secure screen lock.
questions.trap: A numeric PIN is weak compared to biometrics but still far better than a swipe that requires no secret at all.

questions.stem: To stop attackers from guessing the passcode, an iPhone can be configured to do what after 10 failed attempts, and what does this make essential?

choices.text: Erase all data; making a good backup strategy essential
Email the owner; making a strong Wi-Fi password essential
Disable the camera; making MDM essential
Switch to airplane mode; making a SIM PIN essential

questions.explanation: Failed-login-attempt restrictions can erase all data after (for example) 10 failed attempts, which is why a good backup strategy is critical.
questions.trap: The phone wipes itself, not just disables a feature; without backups that data is gone permanently.

questions.stem: Which platform is described as more susceptible to malware because it is more open, versus the closed App-Store-only model of the other?

choices.text: iOS is more open; Android is closed
Android is more open; iOS is a closed App-Store-only environment

questions.explanation: Android is more open, making it more susceptible to malware, whereas iOS is a closed environment where apps come only from the App Store.
questions.trap: The roles are not reversed: iOS is the locked-down one, Android is the more open one.

questions.stem: A phone is lost. Which remote capability uses GPS to pinpoint its location on a map and can play a sound if it's nearby?
questions.explanation: Locator applications use GPS to show the device's location in real time and can remotely play a sound to help find it nearby.
questions.trap: Remote wipe erases data; it does not locate the device on a map.

questions.stem: A stolen phone cannot be recovered and contains sensitive data. Which remote action erases all personal data from the device?
questions.explanation: A remote wipe erases all personal data from a device that cannot be recovered.
questions.trap: Playing a locator sound only helps find a nearby device; it does nothing to protect data on a stolen one.

questions.stem: Why are remote backup applications emphasized for mobile devices?

choices.text: If the device is wiped or replaced, you log into your cloud account and restore your data
They replace the need for a screen lock
They make the phone run faster

questions.explanation: Cloud-based mobile backups constantly save data, so after a wipe or device replacement you just log into your cloud account and your data is restored.
questions.trap: Backups complement, not replace, a screen lock; both are part of mobile security.

questions.stem: Which tool lets corporate admins centrally enforce security policy on both company-owned and BYOD phones, and can push configuration profiles?
questions.explanation: MDM is the central server that enforces security rules across corporate and BYOD devices and pushes configuration profiles (complex passcodes, encryption, disabling the camera, etc.).
questions.trap: A locator app finds a single lost phone; it does not centrally enforce policy across a fleet.

questions.stem: Using an MDM, an admin wants to block the camera whenever employees enter a secure facility. How is this accomplished?

choices.text: By pushing a configuration profile that disables the camera

questions.explanation: Admins use the MDM to push configuration profiles that, for example, force complex passcodes, enable encryption, or disable the camera in secure areas.
questions.trap: A remote wipe erases the whole device; it is far too drastic for simply disabling a camera.

questions.stem: Which maintenance practice for mobile devices is called out as one of the easiest and most important security actions?

choices.text: Keeping both the OS and apps updated through patch management

questions.explanation: Patch management - keeping both OS and app updates current - fixes critical vulnerabilities and is one of the easiest, most important things you can do.
questions.trap: Rooting a device removes built-in protections; it weakens security rather than strengthening it.
